section_summary: This section covers Japanese labor policy and economic recovery in 1948, including proposals to restrict union activity and detailed Mitsubishi shipyard labor agreements and wage tables. It also contains records on newspaper editorial independence, Japanese employment abroad, and the debate over public employees’ bargaining rights. Several correspondents discuss Communist influence in labor unions and the possible appointment of a U.S. labor attaché.

subfiles.title: Comments Regarding the Labor Situation in Japan
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese proposals for labor law changes and introduces three enclosures.
subfiles.summary: The surviving final pages summarize arguments that labor protections hinder productivity and industrial reorganization. Sebald also describes a Mitsubishi collective agreement that sharply limits unilateral management decisions and lists three enclosures.

subfiles.title: Policies to Cope with the Impending Economic Collapse of Japan
subfiles.about: Advocates measures against inflation and labor unrest to support Japanese economic recovery.
subfiles.summary: The study warns of inflation, shortages, falling production, and labor disruption. It calls for removing Communist influence from unions, revising labor laws, temporarily suspending some labor standards, reorganizing industry and government employment, and setting a yen-dollar equivalence. It also seeks relief from occupation expenses and Allied financial assistance linked to wider recovery plans.

subfiles.title: Need of Changing Labor Policy as the Fundamental Prerequisite for Economic Rehabilitation of Japan
subfiles.about: Argues that union powers and labor laws impede Japanese economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.summary: Kitaoka attributes weak productivity and management authority to broad union rights and Communist influence. He urges legal changes allowing dismissal for poor performance, misconduct, sympathy strikes, and Communist activity, along with restrictions on public utility strikes.

subfiles.title: Memorandum Received on the Contract of the Mitsubishi Tokyo Engineering Works
subfiles.from: Mitsubishi Tokyo Engineering Works and Zen Nippon Kiki Trade Union
subfiles.about: Presents a management critique and the text of a Mitsubishi labor contract.
subfiles.summary: The introductory memorandum says the 1946 agreement followed a strike and constrained management. The contract sets union recognition, wage and hour provisions, joint control over personnel decisions and workplace rules, and protections for union and political activity.

subfiles.title: Transmitting Copy of Policy Statement Regarding Application of Press Code to Newspaper Labor Relations
subfiles.from: Acting U.S. Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a SCAP press release on newspaper labor relations.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a release affirming publishers’ responsibility for editorial content under the Press Code.

subfiles.title: Application of Press Code to Newspaper Labor Relations Clarified in Policy Statement
subfiles.from: GHQ Far East Command Public Information Office
subfiles.about: Clarifies management and union rights concerning newspaper editorial content.
subfiles.summary: SCAP assigns editorial decisions to management and permits discipline for attempts to control content by force. It recommends union consultation and impartial review to guard against discriminatory discipline.

subfiles.title: Letter proposing a labor attaché for Japan
subfiles.about: Suggests assigning a U.S. labor attaché amid Japanese labor unrest.
subfiles.summary: Sebald describes strikes and instability, asks Allison to begin identifying a labor attaché acceptable to government and U.S. labor organizations, and plans to prepare the ground with occupation headquarters.

subfiles.title: Means of Obtaining Information on Japanese Labor Developments
subfiles.about: Records Paul Stanchfield’s proposals for obtaining SCAP labor information.
subfiles.summary: Stanchfield proposes informal requests, regular reporting, and a Department visitor to Japan. He expresses interest in a labor attaché post; the memorandum notes earlier SCAP opposition and describes the British attaché’s access.

subfiles.title: Labor Agreements of Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works, and Table of Wages
subfiles.from: U. Alexis Johnson, American Consul General
subfiles.about: Transmits Mitsubishi labor agreements and February 1948 wage tables.
subfiles.summary: Forwards two union agreements, council regulations, and wage tables for the Yokohama works.

subfiles.title: Labor Agreement between Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works and the Salarymen’s Union
subfiles.from: Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works; T. Rinoiye
subfiles.to: Mitsubishi Yokohama Shipyard Salarymen’s Union; K. Yokoo
subfiles.about: Sets union recognition, minimum wages, and joint management consultation for salaried employees.
subfiles.summary: The agreement recognizes the salarymen’s union and creates a Management Council to decide personnel, wage, production, and welfare matters.

subfiles.title: Regulations of Management Council, Salarymen’s Union
subfiles.from: Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works and its Salarymen’s Union
subfiles.about: Defines the membership, authority, meetings, and procedures of the joint Management Council.
subfiles.summary: The rules establish equal company and union representation, monthly meetings, majority votes, confidential proceedings, and binding decisions.

subfiles.title: Labor Agreement between Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works and All Japan Shipbuilding Workers’ Union
subfiles.from: Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works; T. Rinoiye
subfiles.to: All Japan Shipbuilding Workers’ Union, Mitsubishi Yokohama Shipyard Branch; T. Kida
subfiles.about: Sets wages, hours, leave, benefits, union rights, and consultation requirements for shipyard workers.
subfiles.summary: The agreement recognizes the union branch and provides for minimum wages, an eight-hour day, paid leave, medical benefits, and work suspension allowances. It requires negotiation over employment, discipline, production, subcontracting, welfare, and major company changes. It also establishes a Management Council and protects union activity.

subfiles.title: Regulations of Management Council, Shipbuilding Workers’ Union
subfiles.from: Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works and All Japan Shipbuilding Workers’ Union branch
subfiles.about: Defines the joint council’s scope and procedures under the shipbuilding workers’ agreement.
subfiles.summary: The rules give nine seats to each side and cover wages, staffing, production, subcontracting, welfare, and company restructuring. They prescribe meetings, voting, confidentiality, and signed records.

subfiles.title: Wage Rates for Clerks
subfiles.from: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works
subfiles.about: Lists hourly wages and average February salaries for managers and clerks.
subfiles.summary: Tabulates hourly and monthly pay for managers and male and female clerks.

subfiles.title: Average Hourly Wages and Monthly Wages of Laborers, February 1948
subfiles.from: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Yokohama Shipyard and Engine Works
subfiles.about: Details February 1948 pay by shipyard occupation and worker grade.
subfiles.summary: The table lists hourly and monthly wages across numerous trades, four skill classes, apprentices, and total workers, with overall averages.

subfiles.title: Comment on Proposed Policy Decision on Japanese Employment Abroad
subfiles.about: Critiques a proposed policy for Japanese nationals employed overseas.
subfiles.summary: Ray questions assigning oversight to the Japanese government and collecting workers’ earnings above local living costs. He favors simpler clearance and foreign exchange controls and suggests redrafting the policy.

subfiles.title: Draft Policy Decision Acceptable to the United States Government on the Employment of Japanese Abroad
subfiles.about: Proposes rules permitting Japanese nationals to accept overseas employment.
subfiles.summary: The draft sets voluntary employment, individual clearance, wage remittance rules, contract terms, complaint procedures, inspection, and restrictions on political activity and property acquisition.

subfiles.title: Department of State file charge slip, 894.504/7-3048
subfiles.about: Records the circulation of a document filed under 894.504/7-3048.
subfiles.summary: Records file identification, charge information, and a due date.

subfiles.title: Expected Resignation of James S. Killen, Chief of Labor Division, SCAP
subfiles.about: Records AFL and CIO reactions to Killen’s possible resignation over Japanese public employee labor policy.
subfiles.summary: Sullivan recounts Frank Fenton’s objection to MacArthur’s policy and concern that Killen and Paul Stanchfield might resign. James Carey likewise questions limits on collective bargaining for Japanese government employees.

subfiles.title: Communist Influence in Japanese Labor
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, Acting Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Reports Masaji Hitotsumatsu’s views on Communist influence and Japanese labor policy.
subfiles.summary: Sebald summarizes Hitotsumatsu’s belief that occupation labor policies strengthened unions at management’s expense and enabled Communist influence. The despatch links labor instability to fears about investment, economic recovery, and post-occupation security, and cites press support for wider controls on unions.
